common_name: Sunset Coneflower (Coral-Pink Big Sky Series Echinacea)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun; part of the Big Sky series of hybrid coneflowers bred for an expanded color range and tall, sturdy stems.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun. Sunset bears large, single flowers that open a warm coral-orange and fade to soft pink as they age, giving individual plants a two-tone look over the course of bloom, part of the Big Sky hybrid coneflower series bred to move Echinacea colors beyond the classic purple-pink. It flowers heavily from early summer into fall on tall, well-branched stems, drawing bees and butterflies to the broad, flat blooms. Deadhead to prolong flowering, or leave the spiny seed heads standing into winter as forage for goldfinches.

common_name: Twilight Coneflower (Fragrant Rose-Magenta Big Sky Series Echinacea)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun; part of the Big Sky series of hybrid coneflowers, valued for its fragrance and rich rose-magenta flower color.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun. Twilight bears large, richly fragrant, rose-magenta flowers with slightly reflexed petals around a coppery-orange cone, part of the Big Sky hybrid coneflower series and one of the few coneflower cultivars noted for scent as well as color. It blooms from early summer through fall on sturdy stems that rarely need staking, attracting a steady stream of bees and butterflies. Deadhead for continued bloom or leave seed heads standing through winter to feed goldfinches.

common_name: Sombrero Hot Coral Coneflower (Compact Coral-Orange Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, average soil in full sun; part of the Sombrero breeding series selected for compact size, heavy branching, and vivid flower color.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun; Sombrero Hot Coral bears vivid coral-orange flowers with a dark cone on a dense, well-branched, compact plant, part of the Sombrero series bred for heavy bloom without staking. It flowers from early summer into fall and is a strong magnet for bees and butterflies, with the flat-faced blooms making an easy landing pad for pollinators. Deadhead to extend bloom or leave a final flush of seed heads standing for winter bird interest, and divide congested clumps every few years in spring.

common_name: Sombrero Lemon Yellow Coneflower (Compact Bright Yellow Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, average soil in full sun; part of the Sombrero breeding series selected for compact size, heavy branching, and a wide color range.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun; Sombrero Lemon Yellow bears clear, bright lemon-yellow flowers with a dark cone on a dense, compact plant that branches heavily and needs no staking. It blooms from early summer into fall and, like other Sombrero-series coneflowers, attracts abundant bees and butterflies to its flat, daisy-form flowers. Deadhead to prolong bloom, or leave some seed heads standing for winter interest and goldfinch forage, dividing clumps every few years to maintain vigor.

common_name: Sombrero Flamenco Orange Coneflower (Compact Vivid Orange Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, average soil in full sun; part of the Sombrero breeding series selected for compact size, heavy branching, and vivid flower color.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun; Sombrero Flamenco Orange bears saturated, vivid orange flowers with a dark cone on a dense, well-branched compact plant that holds up well without staking. It flowers heavily from early summer into fall, with the bold color and flat bloom form drawing bees and butterflies from a distance. Deadhead to extend the bloom season, or leave a final round of seed heads standing into winter for goldfinches, dividing congested clumps every few years in spring.

common_name: Sombrero Baja Burgundy Coneflower (Compact Deep Wine-Red Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, average soil in full sun; part of the Sombrero breeding series selected for compact size, heavy branching, and deep, saturated flower color.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun; Sombrero Baja Burgundy bears deep wine-red flowers with a dark, almost black-toned cone on a dense, compact plant that branches heavily without staking. Bloom runs from early summer into fall, and the rich, dark color reads well against the more common purple-pink and orange coneflower shades in a mixed planting, while still drawing plenty of bees and butterflies. Deadhead to prolong flowering, or leave some seed heads standing into winter for goldfinches, dividing clumps every few years to renew vigor.

common_name: Double Scoop Bubblegum Coneflower (Fully Double Bright Pink Pompom)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring or fall in well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun; blooms best from well-established container plants and improves in flower production in its second and later years.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil; coneflowers are native prairie plants that struggle in rich, consistently moist ground. Double Scoop Bubblegum produces fully double, pompom-shaped flowers in bright bubblegum-pink with no visible central cone, part of the Terra Nova-bred Double Scoop series developed for dense, dahlia-like double blooms rather than the classic single daisy form. It flowers from summer into fall on a compact, well-branched plant, and while the fluffy doubled flowers offer less accessible pollen and nectar than single coneflowers, bees and butterflies still visit them. Once established the plant is drought-tolerant and needs only occasional division to keep clumps vigorous.

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun; like other Kismet coneflowers, flowers heavily from an early sowing in its first year rather than needing a season to establish.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun; Kismet White bears clean white ray petals around a warm orange-brown cone on a compact, heavily branched plant, part of the Kismet series bred for strong first-year flowering and a tidier habit than many older coneflower cultivars. The pale flowers stand out in the garden at dusk and pair easily with almost any other perennial color. Deadheading extends the bloom season, though leaving some seed heads through fall and winter provides food for goldfinches, and the plant is drought-tolerant once established.
